_about: Fidelia's tool definitions, as Fidelia 2.13.7's own MCP server lists them. Read only by glama/stand-in.js for Glama's build check.
instructions: Fidelia is the person's music player and the library of music they own: their files, their Music app library, any servers they added, and the internet radio stations they keep (stations lists them; play takes a station by name or station_id). You can read all of it, play from it, queue, shuffle, pause and skip, set the volume, say what is playing, and make playlists or add to them. Nothing you do changes or removes a file. Every list comes in pages (limit, offset; next_offset until the end): libraries run to 100,000 tracks, so ask for what you need. A page of tracks is grouped by album (by_album): each album's id, title, artist and whatever all its tracks share (year, genre, composer, date added, disc, format) once, then its tracks with what is their own. search reads plain words as the person said them ("irish trad", "the album I got yesterday", "something by Planxty", "composer Anonymous", "music from 2026") and reports how it read them. Tags often say less than the person means — "Folk" where they mean Irish traditional music — so when search finds too little, read genres, artists_in_genre or composers and use what you know about the music to choose (when a piece was written is the composer's, not the recording's year), then play by album_id, artist or track_ids. Ids are opaque: pass back what a reply gave you.

tools.description: Search the whole library in plain words — a genre, an artist, an album, a song, a composer ("composer Anonymous", "composed by Hildegard"), a year ("2026", "this year") or decade, a date added ("irish trad", "the album I got yesterday", "something by Planxty", "jazz from the fifties"). Answers how the words were read, what play would choose, the albums (each with its whole track count) and artists found, a radio station of that name, and a page of tracks grouped by album (by_album: each album's id, title, artist and whatever all its tracks share — year, genre, composer, date added, disc, format — once, then its tracks with what is their own).
